text: Grandparents had cheap needs and expensive wants. Today it's the reverse.
Black Friday: 30% off. January: 100% of it is due.

Family health insurance through work costs about $28,000 a year.

Most people never see that number.

The company pays about $21,000 of it.

The paycheck covers the rest: about $7,500 a year.

That's roughly $620 a month. Gone before payday even hits.

And that share went up 9% in just ONE year.

Then comes the deductible. Until it's met, every doctor visit is still paid out of pocket.

So families pay $620 a month for insurance...

...and still get a bill every time someone gets sick.

That's not a budgeting problem. That's the system.

Saying "can't afford it right now" out loud might be the most underrated money move.

No fake excuse. No "something came up."

Just: "Skipping dinner out this month. Saving for something."

There's even a name for it now: loud budgeting. 42% of Gen Z already do it.

Why it works:

• Friends stop guessing and start suggesting cheaper plans
• No more spending $80 just to avoid one awkward moment
• Saying the goal out loud makes it real

The right people won't judge it.

They'll suggest a potluck.
